summary: The battery-electric CLA is the first car on Mercedes-Benz's MMA platform and the model that replaces the EQA and EQB as the brand's entry point into electric motoring here. Australian reviewers are near-unanimous that the efficiency and charging hardware are class-leading — an 800-volt system, 320kW DC peak and a 663km WLTP claim on the dual-motor grade — but equally consistent that the car is soft and remote to drive rather than sporting, and that the fastback roofline costs real rear-seat headroom. It reads as a car chosen for range, charging speed and a novated lease that stays inside the FBT exemption, not for driver engagement.
pros: The 350 4MATIC claims 663km WLTP, comfortably ahead of the BMW i4 eDrive35's 448km at similar money
800-volt architecture peaks at 320kW DC, enough to add roughly 300km in about ten minutes — nothing else near this price charges as fast
Both electric grades list below the $91,661 fuel-efficient LCT threshold (the 350 4MATIC by just $361), so a novated lease keeps the FBT exemption
CarExpert matched the 14.4kWh/100km consumption claim on test and rated the ride 'almost pillow-like' for refinement
A 101-litre front boot supplements the 405-litre rear boot, and both grades are rated to tow braked (1500kg and 1800kg)
cons: Rear headroom is tight for anyone over 1.8m and the high battery floor leaves thighs unsupported — the four-door-coupe roofline costs real space
CarExpert's verdict is that it is 'a bit ordinary to drive', with muted steering feel and early understeer even in the 260kW 350 4MATIC
The 800-volt-only design cannot use older 400V-limited DC chargers, including many Australian 50kW units, without the factory DC-DC converter
Mercedes EV resale in Australia has been weak: the EQA and EQB this car replaces both needed repeated local price cuts to sell
Almost every physical control has gone, with MB.OS moving climate and drive functions onto the touchscreens
